CHANGES vs the prior \"v13 Final\" version (which did NOT use the Gate library at all):   1. ADDED \u2014 the Gate's transient flashloan counter now wraps the same open/close window      as the existing `_flashloanInProgress` bool. They serve different purposes and both      stay: `_flashloanInProgress` (+ msg.sender / pool checks) authenticates that a      callback is a legitimate nested call from THIS execute() and not an unsolicited call      from anyone who can trick a real provider into calling back into us; the Gate's      transient counter exists so `finalizeKeyRotation` / `registerStrategy` can assert \"no      flashloan currently open in this contract\" without duplicating that logic. Since      `execute()` is `nonReentrant` and each call opens/closes the counter exactly once,      this only matters as defense-in-depth (e.g. against some future refactor that adds a      second entry path), but it's what the Gate's own docs say it's for.   2. ADDED \u2014 `Gate.requirePostExecutionReconciliation` checks, right before profit is      forwarded to the Vault, that this contract's actual `flashloanToken` balance covers      the `netProfit` the callback claims it computed. Protects against a strategy/callback      bookkeeping bug (`_pendingNetProfit` reporting more than what's actually sitting in      this contract) surfacing as a clear revert here instead of a confusing failure two      calls later inside the Vault's `safeTransferFrom`.   3. ADDED \u2014 `finalizeKeyRotation` and `registerStrategy` now call      `Gate.requirePreRotationReconciliation` (this contract's own flashloan-in-progress      check) AND separately query `IOmegaVault(vault).pendingProofCount()` to confirm the      Vault has no profit stuck mid-flight before a rotation/strategy-upgrade is finalized.      These are two genuinely different pieces of state living in two different contracts \u2014      the Gate cannot see across contracts on its own, so both checks are needed.   4. ADDED (v14.1 \u2014 gas/MEV guard) \u2014 the blueprint now carries a signed `maxBaseFee`      field, and `execute()` reverts with `BaseFeeTooHigh` if `block.basefee` exceeds it.      This is a last-line-of-defense against a blueprint landing after network fee      conditions spike past what the off-chain signer priced in when it computed      `minNetProfit`. It does NOT replace the off-chain gas/profitability engine (blueprint      metadata like `dynamic_min_profit`, `base_fee_at_creation`, and the buffer factors      still do the real work of sizing `minNetProfit` and `maxBaseFee` correctly before      signing) \u2014 it only protects against the gap between \"blueprint signed\" and      \"blueprint included\", where `minNetProfit` alone (a pure token-balance floor) cannot      see gas cost at all. See `maxBaseFee` field docs below for exactly what it does and      does not cover.   5. ADDED (v14.2 \u2014 emergency fund rescue) \u2014 `rescueERC20`/`rescueETH`,      DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE-gated and `nonReentrant`. Closes the \"no-rescue\"      gap: previously any ERC20 dust left after a partial flashloan flow,      or tokens/ETH sent here by mistake or airdrop, were permanently      stranded \u2014 this Orchestrator had no rescue/withdraw/sweep function of      any kind. No encumbrance accounting is needed here (unlike the      Vault's `rescueERC20`) \u2014 see that function's own doc comment for why      any balance found at rest in this specific contract is always safe      to rescue in full. Also asserts `activeFlashloanCount() == 0`      explicitly (redundant with `nonReentrant` today, but makes the      \"never mid-flashloan\" invariant load-bearing rather than an implicit      side effect, per external review \u2014 see the function's own doc      comment). Deliberately does NOT gate on `whenNotPaused`: an emergency      pause is exactly the situation where an admin may most need to move      funds out, so tying rescue to the pause state would be      counterproductive.   6. Everything else \u2014 the real Balancer V2 / Aave v3 / Uniswap V3 flashloan callback      implementations, domain-separated replay protection, chain-scoped nonces, bytecode      integrity checks, dual-key rotation window, strategy registry \u2014 is unchanged from the      prior version. See that version's own header for the full history of why those exist. DESIGN NOTE \u2014 provider handling, per provider type (unchanged from prior version):   - Balancer V2: one admin-configured Vault address (`flashloanProvider`), shared across     all blueprints. Push-repayment: this contract transfers principal+fee back to the     Vault before the callback returns; Balancer checks its own balance increased.   - Aave v3: one admin-configured Pool address (`aavePool`), shared across all blueprints.     Pull-repayment: Aave transfers `amount+premium` FROM this contract via `transferFrom`     after `executeOperation` returns `true`, so this contract must approve the Pool for     that amount before returning, not push a transfer itself.   - Uniswap V3: there is no single canonical pool address \u2014 a different pool exists per     token pair and fee tier, so the blueprint itself must supply `providerContract` (the     specific pool to flash against). This contract determines on-chain whether     `flashloanToken` is that pool's `token0` or `token1` by calling the pool directly,     rather than trusting an off-chain-supplied flag.   Regardless of provider, this Orchestrator still only ever forwards profit to the Vault in   one token per deployment, matching the Vault's own immutable `profit_token` \u2014 checked   explicitly in execute().","events":{"Paused(address)":{"details":"Emitted when the pause is triggered by `account`."},"RoleAdminChanged(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32)":{"details":"Emitted when `newAdminRole` is set as ``role``'s admin role, replacing `previousAdminRole` `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` is the starting admin for all roles, despite {RoleAdminChanged} not being emitted signaling this. _Available since v3.1._"},"RoleGranted(bytes32,address,address)":{"details":"Emitted when `account` is granted `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call, an admin role bearer except when using {AccessControl-_setupRole}."},"RoleRevoked(bytes32,address,address)":{"details":"Emitted when `account` is revoked `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call:   - if using `revokeRole`, it is the admin role bearer   - if using `renounceRole`, it is the role bearer (i.e. `account`)"},"Unpaused(address)":{"details":"Emitted when the pause is lifted by `account`."}},"kind":"dev","methods":{"execute(bytes,bytes)":{"params":{"blueprintCalldata":"ABI-encoded blueprint (see layout above).","sig":"65-byte ECDSA signature over the domain-separated blueprint hash."}},"executeOperation(address,uint256,uint256,address,bytes)":{"details":"Unlike Balancer, Aave v3 PULLS repayment: after this function returns `true`,         the Pool calls `transferFrom(address(this), pool, amount+premium)` \u2014 so this         function must leave a sufficient approval in place, not push a transfer itself."},"finalizeKeyRotation()":{"details":"SNAPSHOT GUARANTEE, NOT AN ATOMIC CROSS-CONTRACT LOCK. `_requireFullReconciliation`         reads `Vault.pendingProofCount()` at one point during this call. So literally any ERC20 balance         found here at rest belongs in one of exactly two buckets: dust         from a strategy that didn't fully sweep back a non-flashloan         token, or an unrelated external transfer \u2014 both rescuable in         full, no encumbrance accounting needed.         `nonReentrant` guarantees this can never be called mid-flashloan         via reentrancy: `execute()` holds the same reentrancy lock for         its entire duration (flashloan open \u2192 strategy \u2192 repay), so this         function cannot be invoked, directly or via a callback, while         borrowed flashloan liquidity is transiently sitting in this         contract. params.sig: 65-byte ECDSA signature over the domain-separated blueprint hash.

executeOperation(address,uint256,uint256.details: Unlike Balancer, Aave v3 PULLS repayment: after this function returns `true`,         the Pool calls `transferFrom(address(this), pool, amount+premium)` — so this         function must leave a sufficient approval in place, not push a transfer itself.

finalizeKeyRotation().details: SNAPSHOT GUARANTEE, NOT AN ATOMIC CROSS-CONTRACT LOCK. `_requireFullReconciliation`         reads `Vault.pendingProofCount()` at one point during this call. Nothing         prevents a new deposit from landing in the Vault in a later transaction,         including one in the same block, immediately after this one finalizes — that         is not a violation of this guard, it's simply outside the epoch this         particular rotation validated against. If stronger synchronization (e.g. a         cross-contract pause during rotation) is ever required, that needs to be         designed in explicitly; this function does not provide it.

flashloanInProgress().details: Should read `false` at the start and end of every top-level transaction —         it's only ever `true` for the duration of a single nested flashloan callback         inside `_executeFlashloan`. A regression spec asserts this stays `false`         across every completed call to this contract; if a future change (e.g. a         `try/catch` added around a provider call) causes a code path to skip the         cleanup at the end of `_executeFlashloan`, that spec is what catches it —         today's EVM revert semantics clear this for free on any reverted path, so this         getter mainly guards against a *successful* path that forgets to reset it.

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

grantRole(bytes32,address).details: Grants `role` to `account`. If `account` had not been already granted `role`, emits a {RoleGranted} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleGranted} event.

paused().details: Returns true if the contract is paused, and false otherwise.

registerStrategy(bytes32,address).details: Only callable by DEFAULT_ADMIN. Frozen strategies cannot be updated. Gated by         full reconciliation — don't swap out strategy code while a flashloan is open         or profit is stuck awaiting release.

renounceRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from the calling account. Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced). If the calling account had been revoked `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must be `account`. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

rescueERC20(address,address,uint256).details: Safe by construction rather than by an explicit balance check:         unlike the Vault, this Orchestrator never carries an intentional,         owed-to-someone-else ERC20 balance between transactions —         `execute()` either forwards 100% of `netProfit` to the Vault and         succeeds, or reverts and leaves no new balance at all (Solidity's         all-or-nothing revert semantics). So literally any ERC20 balance         found here at rest belongs in one of exactly two buckets: dust         from a strategy that didn't fully sweep back a non-flashloan         token, or an unrelated external transfer — both rescuable in         full, no encumbrance accounting needed.         `nonReentrant` guarantees this can never be called mid-flashloan         via reentrancy: `execute()` holds the same reentrancy lock for         its entire duration (flashloan open → strategy → repay), so this         function cannot be invoked, directly or via a callback, while         borrowed flashloan liquidity is transiently sitting in this         contract. The `activeFlashloanCount() == 0` check below is         intentionally redundant with that today — it exists to make the         "never mid-flashloan" invariant an explicit, load-bearing         assertion rather than an implicit side effect of the reentrancy         lock, so it keeps holding even if a future refactor ever adds a         second entry path that doesn't share `nonReentrant`.

rescueETH(address,uint256).details: This contract has no `receive()`/`fallback()`, so a plain ETH         transfer already reverts before ever landing here — but ETH can         still be force-sent via `selfdestruct` from another contract,         bypassing that. This function is the recovery path for exactly         that edge case. Same `activeFlashloanCount() == 0` reasoning as         `rescueERC20` above.

revokeRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from `account`. If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

uniswapV3FlashCallback(uint256,uint256,b.details: Like Balancer, Uniswap V3 expects a PUSH: the pool checks its own post-callback         balance increased by at least amount+fee for whichever token(s) were borrowed.

activeFlashloanCount().notice: This contract's transient flashloan-open counter (EIP-1153). Should read zero         outside of an in-flight `execute()` call.

activeUniswapV3Pool().notice: The Uniswap V3 pool currently authorized to call `uniswapV3FlashCallback`, or         the zero address if none. Same "should always be zero outside of one nested         call" property as `flashloanInProgress()`.

executeOperation(address,uint256,uint256.notice: Aave v3 Pool flashloan callback (IPool.flashLoanSimple). Same         `_flashloanInProgress` reasoning as receiveFlashLoan() above.

finalizeKeyRotation().notice: Finalize key rotation — swaps execution key. Callable at any time after         initiation (see note above); does not require waiting for the window to end.         Gated by full reconciliation — don't hand control to a new key while a         flashloan is open in this contract or profit is stuck awaiting release in the         Vault.

flashloanInProgress().notice: Whether a flashloan callback is currently expected in this transaction.

freezeStrategy(bytes32).notice: Permanently freeze a strategy — cannot be re-activated.

initiateKeyRotation(address,uint64).notice: Initiate key rotation — both old and new keys are valid until windowBlocks         from now, UNLESS finalizeKeyRotation is called earlier (finalizing early is         allowed and immediately revokes the old key — that's an intentional admin         escape hatch, not an oversight).

receiveFlashLoan(address[],uint256[],uin.notice: Balancer V2 Vault flashloan callback. Must only ever be invoked as a nested         call from within `execute()`'s own `flashLoan` call in the same transaction —         `_flashloanInProgress` enforces that, since simply checking `msg.sender ==         flashloanProvider` is not enough: anyone can call the real Balancer Vault's         `flashLoan` naming this contract as recipient with attacker-chosen `userData`,         and Balancer will faithfully call this function with a legitimate         `msg.sender`. The flag closes that hole.

registerStrategy(bytes32,address).notice: Register or update a strategy implementation.

rescueERC20(address,address,uint256).notice: Rescue ERC20 tokens stranded in this contract — dust left over         from a flashloan flow, or tokens airdropped/mistakenly sent here.

rescueETH(address,uint256).notice: Rescue ETH stranded in this contract.

uniswapV3FlashCallback(uint256,uint256,b.notice: Uniswap V3 pool flashloan callback (IUniswapV3Pool.flash). `msg.sender` is         checked against `_activeUniswapV3Pool` rather than a single fixed address,         since (unlike Balancer/Aave) there is no one canonical Uniswap V3 pool.
